scope: Complete supplied four-page main, all four figures, equation 1 and 42-reference bibliography; SI not located/read and cited full sources unreviewed.

bibliographic_scope.title: Asymmetric quantum dot growth via temperature cycling

source_interpretation.topic: Temperature cycling and the comparison routes
source_interpretation.text: The authors cool the reaction after injection to 80 °C and then reheat to 370 °C. They report teardrop CdSe cores and asymmetric head–tail CdSe/CdS rods. Separate constant-370 °C preparations are described as symmetric rods with single emission spectra, but their charges and dwell times are not separately specified.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2–4, Sections 2.3 and 3; Figure 4

source_interpretation.topic: The larger-seed TOP omission is a separate recipe option
source_interpretation.text: The core method states that the separate 1.5 mL TOP addition is omitted for large-size seeds. This does not remove the 1.5 mL TOP used with selenium. No numerical dimension or displayed specimen is explicitly assigned to that variant, so the Figure 2(a) dimensions remain with the representative cycled-core route.

source_interpretation.topic: Particle dimensions do not locate an internal interface
source_interpretation.text: TEM gives core dimensions 10.5 ± 0.7 nm by 6.4 ± 0.4 nm, with aspect ratio 1.7 ± 0.1. For CdSe/CdS rods, the thicker head/stem is 18.3 ± 1.8 nm by 7.7 ± 0.8 nm, with aspect ratio 2.4 ± 0.3; the total length is 44.8 ± 4.1 nm. The authors propose that the head contains the CdSe core. The images do not supply a measured internal interface or shell-thickness map. Approximately 70% are classified as head–tail rods.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 3, Figure 2 and discussion

source_interpretation.topic: Double emission is not proof of two size populations
source_interpretation.text: The purified cores show approximate absorption features at 633 and 580 nm and PL peaks at 582 and 649 nm. No clear bimodal TEM size distribution is observed. After CdS growth the emission peaks shift to about 622 and 663 nm; relative quantum yield rises from about 3% to about 38%. The authors connect the optical behavior to varied faceting or morphology, without resolving separate particle populations.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Figure 1 and discussion

source_interpretation.topic: Wurtzite assignment and the growth model
source_interpretation.text: Powder XRD assigns both cycled products to wurtzite. The source identifies reflections at 35° and 46° as characteristic CdSe <102> and <103>, and describes stronger relative <002> intensity for elongated particles. A shift from bulk CdSe toward CdS is interpreted as shell growth; no numerical refined lattice constant is supplied. The proposed mechanism invokes ligand-limited growth during cooling and renewed anisotropic growth on reheating.

source_interpretation.topic: Two source schematic labels remain unresolved
source_interpretation.text: Figure 4 labels growth <001>, whereas the prose discusses <002>. Its cycle label is 80–370–80 °C, whereas the method records the initial injection, cooling to 80 °C, reheating to 370 °C and room-temperature workup. These are retained as source differences; no silently corrected crystal direction or final 80 °C hold is imposed. The 10 min final anneal is explicit in the core discussion, not independently repeated in the shell procedure.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2–4, Section 2.3, Section 3 and Figure 4

characterization_methods.UV_Vis: Varian Cary100 Bio, 200–900 nm, 8-cell automated holder with Peltier controller.
characterization_methods.TEM: JEOL 2000EX at 100 kV with tungsten filament. Manual particle dimensions and aspect ratios; ImageJ statistics on at least 100 counts.
characterization_methods.XRD: Bruker D8 Advance, Cu Kα wavelength 1.5406 Å, 0.02° steps and 20 s per step. Dried powders on glass slides.
characterization_methods.PL: Excitation 400 nm for quantum dots; spectra in toluene. Spectra corrected for wavelength-dependent excitation and detector response and baseline; emission fitted to a Gaussian profile.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Sections 2.2 and 2.4; Figure 1

optical_concentration_calibration.scope: Illustrative calibration example, not a third measured synthesis sample. Cited calibration methods [36–38] are not independently reviewed.
optical_concentration_calibration.example: A first-band-edge absorption at 555 nm corresponds to approximately 3.17 nm diameter and extinction coefficient 1.86 × 10^5 cm−1 M−1 in the source example. Do not assign these values to the measured 10.5 × 6.4 nm teardrops.
optical_concentration_calibration.relation: Abs = εbc, with b path length and c concentration; actual final batch concentrations unreported.

quantum_yield_calibration.scope: Author relative-comparison method; no equation execution or new estimates.
quantum_yield_calibration.reference_yields: Rhodamine = 31%; rhodamine 6G = 95%, as named by the source. Rhodamine identity is not expanded to a specific isomer here.
quantum_yield_calibration.absorption_control: Prepare samples with optical absorption below 0.05–0.10 to limit inner-filter effects, as printed; no fabricated single threshold.
quantum_yield_calibration.integration: PL_R and PL_qdot are integrated emission areas after source/detector calibration and baseline correction. For samples with lower-energy trap emission, only band-edge emission area is used. Solvent refractive-index correction is included when required.

growth_mechanism.status: Author-proposed interpretation, not measured atomic or interfacial geometry.
steps: Rapid cooling largely quenches initial nucleation and growth.
TOPO capping is proposed to anneal during cooling, limiting growth.
Reheating resumes anisotropic growth and gives teardrop projections.
CdS growth initially occurs on the seed after injection, slows on cooling and extends on reheating.
growth_mechanism.limits: The authors state repeated preparations have similar optical and morphological properties without run counts. Differences in facets or cores remain unresolved; temperature ramp, core-size and anneal-time optimization are proposed future work.
source_label_conflicts: Figure 4 labels the temperature cycle 80–370–80 °C; methods describe cooling from injection to 80 °C, reheating to 370 °C and then room-temperature workup. Preserve the schematic without imposing a final 80 °C hold.
Figure 4 labels growth <001>, whereas the text discusses <002>. Both source labels are retained as author interpretation without a crystallographic correction.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 3–4, Figure 4 and mechanism discussion

cited_background.scope: Introduction and comparative literature are context, not new data from these batches.
cited_background.examples: Literature rod-in-rod quantum yield up to 76% is cited in the Introduction and is not assigned to the present approximately 38% rods.

references.note: Printed bibliography retained, including unusual journal volume/name forms; no external correction or full-reference review.

limitations: Complete four-page supplied main; local filename search found only identical main copies. SI and cited full methods unreviewed.
Inert gas identity, absolute pressure, stirring and many transfer/workup times are not reported. Nitrogen is named only for drying.
The CdSe flask capacity is not stated; the 10 mL four-neck vessel is explicitly a CdSe/CdS shell-growth apparatus.
No final solution concentration, chemical yield, physical batch identifier or atom-resolved interface/coordinates is supplied.
TEM ± values are retained without assigning a standard-deviation/standard-error interpretation. At least 100 particles were analyzed.
The source gives no variant-specific structure for the omitted-extra-TOP large-seed recipe; displayed core data are not duplicated onto it.
Independent source audit passed; presentation remains pending.
